new_statements.quote: 6.2 Stress placement. In general stress falls on the penultimate syllable of words. In the following examples the stressed syllable is underlined: nalun 'food', iliun 'find', kaliran 'spouse'. There are a few exceptions, where often the aspectual clitics -e and -me shift the stress to the ultimate syllable of the root, e.g. mu-falik 'I will-return' but mu-falik-me 'I will-return-ASP'. [p. 115-116] ... [Editor's note, p. 119:] "I know that there are no monosyllabic words in Tugun ... Only after spending more time in the Tugun language did I analyse it as a sequence of like vowels." ... Word stress remains penultimate. --CEQ] [Symbols, p. 119:] Stress in Wetar languages is generally penultimate. It is marked with an apostrophe preceding the stressed syllable where different.

new_statements.relation_note: NOT in the 'works' list (it was opened on 2026-09-16, see); re-read here because it is the source the catalog record itself cites (review.src 'Hinton 2000.. sec. 6.2'). Its penultimate statement is exactly the catalog penultimate stress (penult for 2-6 syllables). Adds two details not in the catalog quote: the compilers note (p. 119) that Tugun has no monosyllabic words and that 'Word stress remains penultimate', and the word-list symbols note that stress in the Wetar languages generally is penultimate. Page locator corrected to pp. 115-116 (catalog gives section only).
new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary stress on the penultimate syllable of the word; the aspectual enclitics -e and -me, when attached, shift stress onto the final syllable of the root (i.e. stress stays penultimate counting the clitic in the domain). No monosyllabic words: apparent monosyllables are sequences of like vowels (VV), so every word has a penult.
new_statements.exceptions: Aspectual clitics -e and -me shift stress to the last syllable of the root (mu-falik vs mu-falik-me), i.e. the clitic counts for stress placement; scanned of the underlined stressed vowels is unreliable (e.g. 'mu-fglik'), so the example transcription should be checked against the PDF image.
new_statements.identity_note: Hinton 2000 describes Tugun as spoken in the Ilway area of Wetar (word list from Ilway); the same paper's survey note says stress is 'generally penultimate' across the Wetar languages (Perai, Aputai, Talur, Tugun, Ili'uun), so the penult reading is island-wide, not a dialect-specific claim. The Hinton 1991 thesis (SIL entry 9665) is on Tugun [tzn], one phonology chapter, but was not obtainable.

audit.action: a better source should be cited for the same classification
audit.reasoning: Coding 'fixed-dominant' penultimate (penultimate stress) with non-strict exceptions matches the source exactly: default penultimate stress, a few exceptions where aspectual clitics -e/-me pull stress to the root-final syllable. The quotation is verbatim at Hinton 2000 sec. 6.2 pp. 115-116 in the copy downloaded now; two further statements in the same paper (p. 119) repeat 'penultimate'. The source is a first-hand sketch by the language's only describer; the only fuller work (his 1991 MA thesis, 157 pp) is print-only and from the same fieldwork, and no later stress/prosody study of Tugun exists in Glottolog or on the web. Hence 'adequate' rather than 'well-sourced' (sketch-level paragraph, fuller thesis unread), no reclassification.
